evidence.experimental_conditions: British Contact Dermatitis Society standard series; readings at D2 and D4; 2005
evidence.support_text: Patch testing using the British Contact Dermatitis Society standard series and Proteks Dry cream as is was performed. D2 and D4 readings reviewed a grade ++ reaction to MDBGN and the cream.

evidence.experimental_conditions: CAPB 1% aqueous (30% active ingredient), 1200 consecutive patients with dermatitis, patch test with European standard series
evidence.support_text: Angelini et al patch tested 1200 consecutive dermatitis patients with CAPB 1% aqueous (30% active ingredient). Positive allergic reactions to CAPB were observed in 46 participants (3.8%).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Coconut diethanolamide 0.5% in petrolatum, Finn chambers, readings at D2 and D3 per ICDRG criteria
evidence.support_text: A 27-year-old non-atopic female with eyelid dermatitis and acrylic artificial nails had a positive patch test to coconut diethanolamide 0.5% pet. (++ at D2 and D3). After removal of the shampoo containing this allergen, the dermatitis cleared.

evidence.experimental_conditions: commercial ointment containing 1% butesin picrate; routine patch test
evidence.support_text: A 15-year-old boy with contact dermatitis from butesin picrate ointment showed a strongly positive reaction (reddening, edema, vesiculation) on routine patch testing with the commercial ointment, which contains 1% butesin picrate.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Cotton twill (1 square inch) treated with 0.1% Octoxynol-9; applied to arms of men and arms and legs of women; secured with adhesive tape; patches remained in place for 6 days; 2-week nontreatment period; new patches applied and removed after 48 h; reading at 2 and 6 days after initial application and 48 h after final application
evidence.support_text: In a study provided by E. I. du Pont de Nemours and Company (1956), the skin sensitization potential of a cotton twill (1 square inch) treated with 0.1% Octoxynol-9 was evaluated using 84 men and 122 women. The test material was applied to the arms of men and to the arms and legs of women. The patches were secured with adhesive tape and remained in place for 6 days. After a 2-week nontreatment period, new patches were applied and then removed 48 h later. Test sites were examined 2 and 6 days after the initial application and 48 h after the final application. No reactions to fabric treated with 0.1% Octoxynol-9 were observed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Crushed azathioprine tablet (Azamun) diluted 1:1 with water; pure azathioprine (Sigma) at 0.1%, 0.1%, and 0.01% in petrolatum
evidence.support_text: Patch testing with crushed azathioprine tablet (Azamun) diluted 1:1 with water produced a positive reaction in a 44-year-old woman with hand dermatitis. The positive reaction was confirmed on serial dilutions from 1:3 to 1:333 in water, and serial dilutions of pure azathioprine at 0.1%, 0.1%, and 0.01% in petrolatum also showed a dose-dependent response.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Dermalibour with Rhealba® Oat Milk cream as is, Finn Chambers on Scanpor, readings at D2 and D3
evidence.support_text: A 3-year-old girl with atopic dermatitis was patch-tested with the suspected cream (Dermalibour with Rhealba® Oat Milk) as is, and showed positive reactions (++) at D2 and D3.

evidence.experimental_conditions: diallyl disulphide 1% to 5%
evidence.support_text: All 4 chefs had positive patch tests to diallyl disulphide at concentrations ranging from 1% to 5%. They presented with dermatitis of the non-dominant hand with hyperkeratosis and fissuring.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Extended European standard series including Anaesthesin® 20% ointment and benzocaine; tested on a 72-year-old woman with dermatitis after herpes zoster treatment; readings at unspecified time showed +++ reaction.
evidence.support_text: Patch tests to an extended European standard series, plus Anaesthesin® 20% ointment and its ingredients, showed +++ reactions to the ointment and to benzocaine. Other ingredients and other local anaesthetics, such as lidocaine, bupivacaine, and procaine, were all negative.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Extended European standard series including bupivacaine; tested on a 72-year-old woman with dermatitis; results negative.
evidence.support_text: Patch tests showed negative reactions to bupivacaine in the same patient.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Finn chambers on Scanpor, 24 h occlusion, readings at 24 and 72 h per ICDRG scoring
evidence.support_text: Patch tests with pure obtusaquinone gave a +++ reaction in a patient who developed allergic contact dermatitis after wearing a wooden necklace containing Cocobolo wood. The +++ reaction indicates strong skin sensitization according to ICDRG scoring.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Finn chambers; 18 healthy volunteers; evaluation at 48, 72, 96 h and 7 days after application of W/O/W emulsion
evidence.support_text: The safety of the W/O/W emulsion (containing rosemary, flaxseed, and oat extracts) was evaluated by human skin patch testing on 18 healthy volunteers. Results were evaluated at 48, 72, 96 h and 7 days after application using Finn chambers. All participants had negative reaction according to the International Contact Dermatitis Research Group criteria, indicating no skin irritation/allergic reaction in vivo.

evidence.experimental_conditions: formulations containing 0.26% to 20.75% diisopropyl adipate, human patch test
evidence.support_text: Formulations containing 0.26% to 20.75% diisopropyl adipate caused minimal to mild irritation but no sensitization in human patch tests.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Grotan® BK 0.15% in water, patch test
evidence.support_text: Rietschel (40) reported on 152 grinders with or without dermatitis of the hands who were patch tested with Grotan® BK 0.15% in water. He found six positive reactions in each group, representing 12% of those with dermatitis and 6% of those without.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Grotan® BK 0.1–1% in water, patch test on over 200 workers
evidence.support_text: Schneider et al. reported patch tests carried out in a total of over 200 workers in contact with Grotan® BK in soluble oil emulsions, 18% of who had dermatitis. Patch tests concentrations of 0.1–1% Grotan® BK in water gave negative results in all subjects (41).

evidence.experimental_conditions: guava tea extract 0.25% aq., readings at D2 and D3, patch tested on a patient with atopic dermatitis
evidence.support_text: Patch testing with guava tea extract 0.25% aq. in a patient with atopic dermatitis showed positive reactions at D2 and D3. 9 healthy controls patch tested with 0.25% guava tea extract were negative.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human patch test; cocamidopropylamine at 0.1% and 0.01% aqueous; 4 participants with dermatitis to CAPB; patch sites read at day 2 and day 4.
evidence.support_text: One participant had a positive reaction that appeared only with cocamidopropylamine (0.1% and 0.01%). The other 2 patients had positive reactions to cocamidopropylamine and CAPB.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human patch test; partially purified CAPB (1% aqueous, containing <0.5% cocamidopropylamine); 4 participants with dermatitis to CAPB; patch sites read at day 2 and day 4 after initial patching.
evidence.support_text: McFadden et al studied 7 participants with dermatitis to CAPB. Four were patch tested with partially purified CAPB (1% aqueous) containing <0.5% cocamidopropylamine and 0.1% and 0.01% cocamidopropylamine. The other 2 patients had positive reactions to cocamidopropylamine and CAPB. Another had a reaction only with CAPB; however irritancy could not be ruled out.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human patch testing using standard series of allergens; patient tested for sensitivity to PPD-related antioxidants.
evidence.support_text: Patch testing revealed sensitivity to PPD-related antioxidants used in black rubber, and a manufacturer of EHRs confirmed that these antioxidants are present in the finished product. This provides evidence that contact with an exercise hand rest (EHR) containing IPPD (0.5%) and DPPD (1.0%) caused the patient's unilateral palmar hand dermatitis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human; 5 subjects with occupational dermatitis; Patch test with 0.1% glutaraldehyde.
evidence.support_text: In a study of cleaning staff with dermatitis using Cidex, three of five patients reacted to 0.1% glutaraldehyde in patch tests.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human; 5 subjects with occupational dermatitis; Patch test with 0.5% glutaraldehyde.
evidence.support_text: In a study of cleaning staff with dermatitis using Cidex, three of five patients reacted to 0.5% glutaraldehyde in patch tests.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human; 5 subjects with occupational dermatitis; Patch test with 1% glutaraldehyde.
evidence.support_text: In a study of cleaning staff with dermatitis using Cidex, all five patients reacted to 1% glutaraldehyde in patch tests.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Human; 5 subjects with occupational dermatitis; Patch test with 2% formaldehyde.
evidence.support_text: In a study of cleaning staff with dermatitis using Cidex, two of five patients reacted to 2% formaldehyde in patch tests.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Indian standard series (ISS); reading per ICDRG guidelines; tested in suspected ACD patients.
evidence.support_text: Positive reaction exclusively in males was seen with ... mercapto mix, ... black rubber mix ...

evidence.experimental_conditions: Induction phase: 4 h exposure; challenge phase: 24 h exposure; test site: upper arm; vehicle/formulation: female sexual hygiene product containing CBD from cannabis extract
evidence.support_text: In the human skin sensitization test for the female sexual hygiene product containing CBD from cannabis extract, during the induction phase there was no observed skin irritation or redness at the test site across all evaluated time intervals. In the challenge phase, no immediate irritation was observed right after removal of the patch in 76.67% of participants; minimal erythema that was barely perceptible was observed in 23.33% immediately after removal and decreased to 10% at 8 h post-removal. Any irritation symptoms normalized within 24 h. The authors state that no allergic reactions were observed.

evidence.experimental_conditions: lowest concentration that elicited a reaction
evidence.support_text: Baadsgaard and Jorgensen reported that a 41-year-old female cleaner had developed a red, pruritic, papular, sometimes urticaria-like eruption on the face, hands and the distal part of the arms after having used a new BYD-containing cleaning agent for a few months, and patch testing with BYD elicited a positive reaction at a certain concentration; 55 controls were negative even at a tenfold higher concentration.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Methotrexate Lederle® (1 vial, 25 mg/ml) tested as is; patches applied for 2 days, reading on day 7. Ten healthy controls tested with the same preparation, all negative.
evidence.support_text: On day 7, the methotrexate patch (tested as is) produced papules, edema, erythema, and pruritus, with a + reaction, while ten healthy controls showed no reaction, indicating positive skin sensitization to methotrexate.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Occlusive forearm patches with 2%, 4%, and 6% fluridil, applied for 21 days
evidence.support_text: Neither fluridil nor isopropanol showed sensitization/irritation potential, unlike vaseline. In the study, occlusive forearm patches with 2, 4, and 6% fluridil were applied to 20 men for 21 days.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Occlusive patches moistened with 0.4 ml test solution applied to upper arms of 59 men and women (age 21–60). Induction: patches applied on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays for 3 consecutive weeks, removed at 24 h post-application. Challenge: duplicate applications after a 2-week nontreatment period, scored at 48 and 96 h post-application.
evidence.support_text: Both Acetyl Triethyl Citrate and Acetyl Tributyl Citrate were nonirritating to the skin, and reactions suggestive of contact sensitization were not observed during the study (Hill Top Research 1978). A total of 59 men and women (age 21–60) participated; occlusive patches moistened with 0.4 ml test solution were applied to the upper arms on Mondays, Wednesdays, and Fridays for 3 weeks, with removal after 24 h. Challenge patches were applied after a 2-week nontreatment period and scored at 48 and 96 h.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Open and unoccluded patch test with Acute Kare hand soap; test subject: patient with hand, face and neck dermatitis.
evidence.support_text: A 41-year-old nurse with hand, face and neck dermatitis had open and unoccluded patch tests showing a +3 bullous reaction to Acute Kare hand soap manufactured by Steris Company. The patient's symptoms resolved upon discontinuing use of the soap.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch containing ethylhexyl dimethyl PABA dissolved in 4% white Vaseline affixed to adult volunteers.
evidence.support_text: A patch containing ethylhexyl dimethyl PABA dissolved in 4% white Vaseline® affixed to adult volunteers did not cause skin sensitization (3).

evidence.experimental_conditions: patch test concentration not specified
evidence.support_text: Five of the 13 cases were considered as sequelae of a contact dermatitis due to OPP and PPP. Patch tests with both compounds were made on three patients, but only one case proved OPP positive (Ito et al., 1968).

evidence.support_text: Patch test results (Table) show 2 allergic reactions to fenvalerate among 230 subjects; these patients had chronic hand dermatitis.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test for cell-mediated hypersensitivity; test concentration not stated; paraffin control; three patients tested.
evidence.support_text: Four Castor Wax extracts and paraffin (control) were evaluated in patch tests for cell-mediated hypersensitivity. None of the three patients had a delayed reaction to any of the four Castor Wax extracts (test concentration not stated).

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test in psoriasis patients; 74 patients tested.
evidence.support_text: Out of 74 psoriasis patients, 13 reported that they were allergic to Coal Tar, but only 2 had a positive patch test.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test on a 45-year-old female patient with face dermatitis lasting three months after using Avène® 20B 7A cream.
evidence.support_text: A case of allergy to Euxyl K 400 contained in an Avène® 20B 7A cream caused face dermatitis for three months in a 45-year-old female patient; patch test to the cream or its components was positive for Euxyl K 400 and negative for phenoxy-ethanol.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test on a 64-year-old woman with gradually worsening recurring dermatitis after using Vichy® Capital Soleil cream.
evidence.support_text: A 64-year-old woman had gradually worsening recurring dermatitis after using Vichy® Capital Soleil cream; patch testing identified ethylhexylglycerine as the responsible agent.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test on a 64-year-old woman with widespread contact dermatitis after applying a sunscreen product.
evidence.support_text: A 64-year-old woman developed widespread contact dermatitis after applying a sunscreen product; patch testing revealed positive reactions to isohexadecane, which was one of the responsible agents.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test on a 64-year-old woman with widespread contact dermatitis after applying a sunscreen product.
evidence.support_text: A 64-year-old woman developed widespread contact dermatitis after applying a sunscreen product; patch testing revealed positive reactions to isopropyl myristate, which was one of the responsible agents.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test on a 67-year-old woman with a history of pruriginous eruption on arms and legs related to sun exposure, using a SP with SPF 25.
evidence.support_text: A 67-year-old woman with a pruriginous eruption on arms and legs related to sun exposure had positive patch tests to her sunscreen and to the tetrahydroxypropyl ethylene diamine it contained.

evidence.experimental_conditions: Patch test on a 73-year-old man with face and neck dermatitis after using a photoprotective lotion.
evidence.support_text: A 73-year-old man developed face and neck dermatitis from a photoprotective lotion; patch testing identified polyethylene glycol-7 hydrogenated castor oil as the only positive ingredient.

evidence.experimental_conditions: parabens in alcohol/water mixture
evidence.support_text: The panelist was then exposed to the components of the products: parabens in alcohol/water mixture, disodium EDTA in water, chloroxylenol in yellow petrolatum, dihydroabietyl alcohol in yellow petrolatum, the water phase, and the oil phase of the product. The subject was definitely sensitized to parabens and chloroxylenol.

evidence.experimental_conditions: NACDG diagnostic series; patient population
evidence.support_text: Diagnostic tests for skin sensitization show a reaction rate of 3% by the NACDG for parabens.
Adams and Maibach (1985) patch-tested 713 patients with cosmetic-related reactions and identified 19 individuals with positive reactions to unspecified parabens.
Among patients with a positive patch test to PPDA, 8 showed positive reactions to paraben mix: 3 with PPDA grade +, 3 with grade ++, and 2 with grade +++ (Table VII).
Another case in Mowad (2000) involved a 40-year-old woman with hand rash; patch testing revealed a positive reaction to paraben-mix.

Carradori et al. (1990) reported that patch tests with a standard series identified positive reactions to paraben-mix at 48 and 72 h in a 65-year-old woman with systemic contact dermatitis following ampicillin injection.
Cooper and Shaw (1998) reported a case of a 74-year-old female with allergic contact dermatitis from parabens in a tar shampoo; patch testing revealed positive reactions to paraben mix.
Table II shows that 8 patients had positive patch test reactions to paraben mix, representing 4.8% of the positive group. Reaction grades were + in 6 and ++ in 2 patients.
